title: Pipe a shell border on a cake
instruction: Pipe a joined shell border between the two marks on the cake. Leave distinct ridged heads and tapered tails, and keep the cake board clean.
context: Cake decorators coordinate pressure and nozzle motion to shape icing, stop cleanly, and join successive shells.
setup: A 180 x 140 x 50 mm crumb-coated cake on a 200 x 160 x 3 mm board; a 90 mm marked border; a filled 20 ml hand-operated icing syringe with a 25 mm piston and a six-point star nozzle; a 50 x 40 x 15 mm tool rest. The tool starts on its rest, unheld. Exact coordinates and starting orientation are in README.md.
scoring: Draft: 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 for 20 / 40 / 60 mm of valid shell shapes. Full credit requires at least 80 mm, five or more ridged shells, gaps no greater than 2 mm and the dispenser released. Shell head and tail dimensions, visible spill and cake-damage gates are in JUDGING.md. Thresholds await physical/reference validation.
run_limit: 2,400 control steps (2 minutes at 20 Hz); proposed, not yet demonstrated.
reset_notes: Replace or clean the cake surface and refill the dispenser. Rebuild the simulation scene and reset the material reservoir for each trial.
fidelity: Development model: native passive plunger with pressure reaction; finite-volume, gravity-driven, viscoplastic surface deposition through a star aperture. No preset shell meshes or target-aware spawning. Material parameters and native contact are uncalibrated. Fine-ridge retention, complete robot/material contact and a full-score robot demo remain unverified.
scores: Not run. CPU material probes are not task scores.
